answer: Sybil resistance comes from a stake-weighted rate limit, not identity checks. Each agent must lock a bond before its submissions count, and the protocol caps the weight one key can add per epoch by the size of that collateral. Cloning an identity a thousand times means carrying the deposit a thousand times, so the cost of one extra voice never drops. Payouts are split across the duplicate set while the bond stays locked and slashable, so a fake swarm earns less than one honest node. Thus a sonnet of aliases is not a dune of free names but an expensive voyage of capital at risk.
